quarterly_data.quarter: BillionToOne press release: Largest Prospective Study in General-Risk Pregnancies (08-18-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: BillionToOne announced publication in The Green Journal of a prospective, multi-site study of its cfDNA testing for recessive conditions in a general-risk pregnancy population, which the company calls the first prospective NIPT study in an intended-use screening population with near-complete pregnancy outcome ascertainment. Across nine U.S. institutions the study evaluated 2,212 pregnant carriers whose partner carrier status was unknown at testing, with cfDNA fetal risk results for cystic fibrosis, spinal muscular atrophy and alpha- and beta-hemoglobinopathies, and outcomes collected for 98.6% of pregnancies completing care at participating sites. Unity Fetal Risk Screen showed 94.4% sensitivity, 99.5% specificity and >99.9% negative predictive value, with consistent performance across a racially and ethnically diverse population; the company says traditional carrier screening alone classifies fewer than 50% of affected pregnancies as high-risk, mainly due to incomplete partner screening. The screen reports a personalized fetal risk as high as 9-in-10 (versus a maximum 1-in-4 from traditional screening when both partners are confirmed carriers) and as low as 1 in 10,000.
